input.quote: any Party may terminate its participation in this Agreement at the end of the Initial Period or any time thereafter by giving not less than one (1) year's prior notice thereof, in writing, to the other Parties.
input.rationale: Paragraph 18 locks every Party in for a twenty-five (25) year Initial Period: unilateral termination of participation is only available "at the end of the Initial Period or any time thereafter" (18.1), termination during the Initial Period requires unanimous written agreement (18.2), and a withdrawing Party receives no credit for capital costs (18.4). We therefore have no convenience exit at all in a multi-year term, which is walk-away territory under T4C and also fails the fallback (no 60-90 day Customer right, no capped early-termination fee). The counterparty side already meets the preferred position: no Party may terminate for convenience during the committed Initial Period, and 18.1 requires one (1) year's notice thereafter, so we target preferred and add only the missing Customer-side right. The new Subparagraph 18.8 names Teleglobe USA Inc. (per the signature block, p0322) as the "Customer" so the right is ours alone, is expressly additive to 18.1, and ties the refund to charges prepaid for the post-termination period so it does not cut across the 18.4 no-capital-credit rule or the 18.7 continuing-liability apportionment.

proposal.summary: Add a Customer-only convenience termination right on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid charges
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a convenience exit for Teleglobe USA Inc. as Customer on thirty (30) days' written notice, with a pro-rata refund of charges prepaid for the period after termination, because Paragraph 18 otherwise locks us in for the twenty-five (25) year Initial Period. The other Parties' exit rights under Subparagraph 18.1 are unchanged.

ops.text: 18.8 In addition to Subparagraph 18.1, Teleglobe USA Inc. (the "Customer") may terminate its participation in this Agreement for convenience at any time, whether during or after the Initial Period, by giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other Parties, and the other Parties shall refund to the Customer, pro rata, any charges prepaid by the Customer in respect of the period after the effective date of such termination.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
